Explore trajectory diagnostics with the scans app

Source: R/scans-app.R
scans_app.Rd

scans_app() launches a Shiny app for exploring one or more TrajectoryBundle snapshots or saved investigation_snapshot() values. A named list creates an application switcher; each entry can be a bundle, saved investigation, or a zero-argument loader that returns either. Lazy loaders make it practical to review snapshots from multiple deployed apps without downloading every snapshot when the review app starts.

Usage

scans_app(
  x,
  annotations = NULL,
  investigations = inherits(x, "scans_investigation"),
  reviews = FALSE,
  chat_factory = NULL,
  scanners = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A TrajectoryBundle, a saved investigation_snapshot(), a comparison from compare_trajectories(), or a named list of application sources. Each source can be a bundle, a saved investigation, or a zero-argument function that returns one. Source names are shown in the application switcher.

annotations

Optional scans_annotations() store. When supplied, the app shows an annotation panel for the selected trajectory and appends what reviewers write to that store. The store also supplies current annotation filter membership when opening a saved investigation. Without a store, saved membership is used and the app writes only explicitly requested investigation downloads.

investigations

Whether to enable investigation save, upload, and rescan controls. Defaults to TRUE for a single saved investigation and FALSE for other inputs. Set explicitly for named sources or lazy loaders.

reviews

Whether to enable session-local evidence review and example export controls. Defaults to FALSE. Download selected examples to keep them after closing the session; no shared review store is written.

chat_factory

Optional zero-argument function returning an ellmer chat, for example function() ellmer::chat_openai(). Defaults to NULL, which omits Ask. Tools configured on this client are replaced with the bounded scans tools; its system prompt is retained with evidence instructions.

scanners

Optional custom scanners: one scanner() or a list of them. They appear with the built-in scans in Options, run with them on the loaded bundle, and their findings and assessment status are shown the same way. A saved investigation shows its saved custom results without them; applying current scanners reruns only the scanners supplied here. Scanners that could never run are refused rather than ignored: with a single saved investigation opened with investigations = FALSE, and with a comparison, whose sides are the saved analyses it compares (rerun each side with investigation_snapshot() and compare again). Custom scanners are deterministic functions, so browsing never calls a model.

Value

A shiny::shinyApp() object. Calling scans_app() at the console launches the app; the returned object can also be served from an app.R.

Details

The scans app keeps the canonical bundle as its data boundary. Ordinary inspection does not call a model, replay tools, or modify a bundle. Caller-supplied loaders are invoked only when their application is first selected in a session or explicitly reloaded.

The app opens with an overview of the trajectories in view. Stat tiles state counted facts with their denominators: how many are in view, how many have findings out of those a scan could assess, how many tool calls failed, and median elapsed time and tokens with the number of records that carry each. An activity chart shows them by start day or hour, patterns list each finding type with its reach and trend, and tables break the cohort down by tool, model, and user. Every count is a control: selecting a bar, pattern, tool, user, or model narrows the overview, the browser, and Ask together, and the active filters appear as removable chips. Elapsed time includes any pauses between user messages and is not model response latency. Unknown measurements remain unknown, and no findings is not evidence of success.

Selecting a trajectory opens a source-neutral transcript and event stream with the findings, evaluations, and adapter losses recorded for it. Built-in findings are computed with scan_trajectories() when each application snapshot is first loaded.

Review queue and dispositions

With an annotations store the browser is a review queue. Entries show why they are flagged and whether they are reviewed, and "Needs review" orders them by a fixed rule (unreviewed first, then error findings, warnings, unassessed, and clean, newest first) rather than a score. A bar above the transcript marks the open trajectory with one of the store's labels, or as reviewed without a label, by button or by key (1-9, E); U opens the next unreviewed trajectory and ? lists the shortcuts. Each mark appends one record to the store; nothing is edited or deleted. Without a store the app is read-only and claims no review state.

Exports

The overview's Export menu offers the trajectories and findings in view as CSV, a report, and an R snippet that rebuilds the snapshot and scan settings. The report is the one investigation_report() produces, as a standalone HTML file or as Markdown to paste into an issue: for an opened investigation the app and a script give the same report. It names every active filter, carries counts with their denominators and the evidence identities behind each pattern, and contains no transcript text, and user identifiers and recorded error text only when requested. A single trajectory can be copied as Markdown, which does contain its content. Links are the app's own address with the trajectory and every active filter, and opening one clears any filter it does not set. They select whatever matches those filters where they are opened, and the report states what a link cannot restore. No export contains credentials.

Deputy runs and provenance

For Deputy runs the header states the recorded run ending, including an answer the provider cut short on a run whose status is still completed, and links a delegated run to its lead through the recorded lineage. The overview lists run interventions by kind. A Deputy result's usage includes its delegated runs at every level, while a trace records each run's own model calls; token totals count each delegated run once either way. For sources that record commons provenance, the overview counts exchanges as trusted, cited, untrusted, or unclassified, and ranks recurring exploratory tool routes as candidates for governed measures, with the recorded tool input and output shown as text and never executed.

Ask about the evidence

Supply chat_factory to enable an optional Ask tab beside Findings. It must return an ellmer chat configured with your chosen provider. Each session clones the client, clears its prior turns and tools, and registers only scans_tools(). Provider requests begin when the user submits a question. The permitted trajectories and snapshot are fixed at submission; browsing while a response streams cannot change them. Changing scope starts fresh model context while keeping earlier answers and drafts visible. Links in older answers open their retained snapshot, with a return-to-source action. Chat history and evidence references last only for the current session. The provider receives the submitted question and any retained evidence its tools read. Existing redactions remain intact; no new anonymization occurs. A recent shinychat with page_chat_theme() and chat_server()$set_client() is required for this surface.

Saved investigations

Set investigations = TRUE to enable save/open controls in a regular app. They are enabled by default when x is a single saved investigation. Save visible trajectories downloads the selected retained evidence, analysis, scanner settings, and browser state as JSON. The preview describes the content policy before download. Open an investigation restores a file in the current session. Saved diagnostics remain unchanged until the reviewer chooses Apply current scanners; saving again records a parent revision. Opening does not contact the original source. The default upload limit is 50 MiB. An explicit shiny.maxRequestSize option sets both the app upload ceiling and its investigation reader limit; Inf disables the size limit. See investigation_files().

Comparisons

Pass a compare_trajectories() result to open a comparison. The baseline and candidate investigations become the two applications in the switcher, and the overview leads with the comparison: what could not be compared first, then the matched cases, which can be narrowed to regressions, improvements, pattern changes, resource changes, or cases with something not comparable. Each case links to both trajectories and to the events its findings cite. Every number shown is read from the comparison value.

A comparison is a fixed pair of saved analyses. With investigations = TRUE a side's visible trajectories can be saved, but the app offers no opening of another investigation and no "Apply current scanners", so each side keeps the analysis the comparison reports. Ask evidence from the other side switches to that side, and a comparison link leaves any investigation opened over a side.

Posit Connect

Use scans_app_connect() when Connect content observability is enabled. It reads native OTLP traces for named deployed applications and supplies the lazy loaders used by the application switcher. Custom loaders remain useful for completed snapshots held outside Connect's trace store.

Examples

bundle <- TrajectoryBundle(
  data.frame(
    trajectory_id = "trajectory-1",
    source_type = "manual"
  ),
  data.frame(),
  data.frame()
)

if (interactive()) {
  scans_app(bundle)

  scans_app(list(
    "Support assistant" = bundle,
    "Research assistant" = function() readRDS("research-bundle.rds")
  ))
}
